title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act establishes rules for using artificial intelligence in processing veterans’ claims, aiming to protect beneficiaries and ensure fair treatment. It focuses on transparency, accountability, and safeguards to prevent bias or errors in AI-assisted decisions.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 is a proposed law that requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to clearly disclose the use of artificial intelligence in its services. It aims to ensure veterans are informed about how AI influences decisions that affect their care and benefits.

title: To prohibit Chinese AI models from being used on government-issued devices or software systems, to prohibit the procurement of any such models, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: This policy forbids any Chinese AI models from being installed or run on devices and software systems issued by the government. It also bars the government from purchasing or otherwise acquiring these models for any purpose.

title: To establish age-appropriate design standards and safety safeguards for artificial intelligence chatbots accessed by minors, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy sets guidelines for designing AI chatbots so they are safe for children to use. It requires developers to add age‑appropriate features and safety safeguards to protect minors and other users.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This act establishes a public awareness and education campaign to inform citizens about artificial intelligence. It aims to promote understanding of AI’s benefits, risks, and responsible use through public programs, resources, and collaboration with stakeholders.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 establishes a framework for assessing and managing the risks associated with AI systems. It requires developers and users to evaluate potential harms, implement safety measures, and report findings to ensure AI technology is deployed responsibly.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: The resolution creates a new Select Committee focused on artificial intelligence. Its purpose is to oversee AI policies, review developments, and recommend guidelines for responsible use.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a legislative proposal aimed at establishing clear guidelines for the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence technologies. It seeks to promote transparency, accountability, and safety in AI systems while fostering innovation and protecting citizens' rights.

title: A bill to require the Secretary of Defense to establish reporting requirements and voluntary guidance for large artificial intelligence contractors.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Armed Services.
summary: This bill requires the Secretary of Defense to set up reporting requirements for large artificial‑intelligence contractors. It also establishes voluntary guidance to help those contractors meet defense AI standards.

title: A bill to provide for the retraining and support of workers displaced by automation technologies or artificial intelligence, to require Federal action during periods of elevated unemployment, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: This bill aims to help workers whose jobs are replaced by automation and AI by offering retraining programs and support services. It also mandates the federal government to take action during times of higher unemployment to protect affected workers.

title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate regarding the importance of religious freedom, authoritative texts, and transparency in artificial intelligence systems.
action: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4958; text: CR S4951)
summary: The Senate’s resolution stresses that artificial intelligence systems must respect religious freedom and be guided by authoritative texts, while remaining transparent. It urges policies that ensure AI development and deployment align with these principles.

title: A bill to establish the Artificial Intelligence Safety Board, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This bill proposes the creation of an Artificial Intelligence Safety Board to oversee AI development, safety, and ethical standards. It also includes additional provisions for regulation, public oversight, and related AI policies.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is a policy framework designed to safeguard consumers from misleading or deceptive artificial intelligence technologies. It establishes guidelines for transparency, labeling, and accountability to ensure that AI systems cannot deceive users or exploit them.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 is a law designed to improve the safety and reliability of AI systems. It establishes guidelines, funding, and oversight to ensure that AI research and development meet high standards of performance, transparency, and public trust.

title: To direct the Director of National Intelligence to submit to Congress a report on the use of artificial intelligence systems to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This policy directs the Director of National Intelligence to provide Congress with a report on how artificial intelligence systems are used to gather, analyze, query, or share information under Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. The report will cover the deployment of AI for acquiring or accessing intelligence data in that context.

title: Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This act is designed to improve education and training in artificial intelligence so that workers are prepared for the growing AI industry. It encourages collaboration between schools, employers, and the government to develop curricula, certifications, and job programs that match current and future AI job needs.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 26 - 21.
summary: The Open-Source AI Leadership Act aims to promote the creation and use of open‑source artificial‑intelligence tools and models, encouraging transparency and collaboration across industry, academia, and government. It seeks to position the United States as a global leader in AI by mandating that federally funded AI research be released under open‑source licenses and by providing incentives for private sector partners to share their AI innovations.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 establishes regulations that require medical diagnoses, treatment plans, and patient care to be performed by licensed human doctors rather than by artificial intelligence systems. It aims to protect patient safety and ensure a personal, accountable standard of care by limiting the use of AI in clinical decision‑making.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 is designed to prevent companies from using AI tools to inflate prices and manipulate wage levels unfairly. It proposes new regulations that would require transparent pricing and fair labor practices in AI-driven industries.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: This policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, through the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to create a pilot program that uses AI to protect critical infrastructure from cyber attacks. It also includes additional measures aimed at strengthening overall cybersecurity for essential services.

title: A bill to establish the Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This bill proposes creating the Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations to oversee, investigate, and address cybersecurity and artificial intelligence concerns. It also includes additional provisions to support related purposes and ensure accountability.

title: A bill to establish the Artificial Intelligence Horizon Fund, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The bill proposes creating a new Artificial Intelligence Horizon Fund to support research, development, and deployment of AI technologies. It also includes additional provisions to guide AI governance, promote innovation, and address related policy issues.

title: READ AI Models Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The READ AI Models Act is a proposed law that would establish rules for how AI models are created, used, and shared, aiming to make sure they operate safely and ethically. It would likely require developers to disclose key details about their models, such as training data and intended applications, so that regulators and the public can understand and assess their impact.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act is designed to shield households from the rising utility bills caused by the power hungry AI data centers. It proposes measures such as setting limits on energy charges, encouraging efficiency upgrades, and increasing oversight to keep energy costs affordable for families.

title: Department of Advanced Technology and Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: The Department of Advanced Technology and Artificial Intelligence Act creates a new federal agency tasked with overseeing the development, regulation, and deployment of cutting‑edge technology and AI systems. The act outlines the department’s role in promoting innovation, ensuring national security, safeguarding privacy, and establishing ethical standards and oversight mechanisms for AI research and applications.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 seeks to make sure that AI systems used in veteran services are developed and deployed in a safe, fair, and transparent way. It sets up guidelines and oversight mechanisms to protect veterans from potential harms or biases while still encouraging the use of innovative AI solutions.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act is proposed legislation aimed at preventing the creation and use of autonomous AI systems that could pose significant risks to public safety, privacy, or national security. It seeks to establish regulatory safeguards, oversight mechanisms, and penalties to ensure that AI technology is developed and deployed responsibly and within legal bounds.

title: Covered AI Prohibition Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The Covered AI Prohibition Act bans the use of AI systems that could be harmful or deceptive, requiring clear transparency and safeguards for any AI that might manipulate users or spread misinformation. It imposes strict regulatory oversight and penalties for noncompliance on all AI tools that fall within its coverage.
